 KIRTIBHAI REVABHAI PATEL NAMED IN THE FIR AS DR. KIRTIBHAI  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT  ================================================================
 Appearance:

sentences.text: MR PR ABICHANDANI(102) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MS MONALI H BHATT, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1

This petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, 1950 read with the provisions of Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as the "Cr.P.C") for quashing and setting aside FIR being I-C.R. No.2 of 2014 registered with Ranavav Police Station,
District Porbandar for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as "the Code") read with Sections 19, 23(1)(c), (e), (f), (g), (i) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").

2. Heard learned advocate Mr P.R. Abichandani for the petitioner and learned APP Ms. Monali H.
Bhatt for the respondent-State.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined
3. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and with consent of the learned advocates for the the respective parties, this matter is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

4. The brief facts of the case are as under:-

sentences.text:
The allegations of the complainant against the accused person/s in the impugned FIR are that when the officials of the respondent-State were on patrolling and reached at Mokar Village Patia, they were informed about an illegal stock exchange,
which was being run by one Mr. Pankaj Nanjibhai Rana in his shop named "A-one Store".
Thereafter, a raid was carried out at the premises in presence of two panchas.
It is alleged in the impugned FIR that certain articles were recovered and a person was found in the premise where the raid was carried out.
After the aforesaid raid, the First Information Report being FIR I-C.R.2 of 2014 was filed by the complainant on 10.01.2014 with Ranavav Police Station, District-Porbandar.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined

Hence, FIR /
complaint came to be registered against the petitioner and other accused.

5. Learned advocate for the applicant submits that impugned FIR is nothing but a clear abuse of the process of law mainly on two grounds; first, the ingredients of Section 420 of the Code are not attracted and there are no allegations, whereby the present applicant can be roped for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Code.

Secondly, the provisions contained under Section 26 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, are not attracted and a charge-sheet could not have been filed for the alleged offence punishable under the said Act.
5.1. Learned advocate for the applicant while elaborating his submissions further submits that petitioner has not traded in securities / stocks through accused No.1.
It is further submitted that the present applicant who is accused No.5, is a small time investor and the applicant used to make small investments in shares with a sub-borker of Angel Broking.

It is further NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined submitted that accused No.1 is a registered sub-broker of Angel Broking Private Limited and a certificate of registration is also placed on record at page No.30 of the compilation.
Learned advocate for the applicant has relied upon the statements issued by the Angel Broking and submitted that since 2008 onwards, the applicant is in the trading of the shares and securities.

Learned advocate for the applicant has relied upon the decision of the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Vipulkumar Avantilal Shah Versus State of Gujarat delivered on 15.03.2018 in Special Criminal Application No.1781 of 2018 by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court.

entities.text: Vipulkumar Avantilal Shah Versus State of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5.2. By relying upon the above decision, the learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that Section 26 of the Act envisages that no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act or any rules or regulations or bye-laws made thereunder, save on a complaint made by the Central Government or State Government or the Securities and NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined Exchange Board of India or a recognised stock exchange or by any person.
It is further submitted that in the present case, the complainant is a Police Sub-Inspector.
It is further submitted that the impugned FIR does not disclose any ingredient for invoking the provisions of Section 420 of the IPC.

It is therefore,
submitted that the impugned FIR may be quashed and set aside.

5.3. During the course of hearing of the matter, the learned advocate for the applicant has placed on record the compilation of charge-sheet papers qua co-accused in compliance of the order dated 16.07.2024 passed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, which is taken on record.

Per contra, learned APP Ms. Monali H. Bhatt for the respondent-State has placed on record the investigation report dated 11.12.2024 duly signed by the Police Inspector Ranava Police Station.
The same is taken on record.

It is submitted by the learned APP that so far as the accused Nos.1 to 4 are NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined concerned, after the completion investigation of investigation, charge-sheet No.I-12 of 2014 dated 03.04.2014 was filed and the learned Magistrate Court, Porbandar has committed case.
Case is registered as Sessions Case No.01 of 2015.

It is further submitted that during the proceedings, the accused Nos.1 to 4 were discharged from the commission of an offence under Sections 19, 23(1)(c), (e), (f), (g), (i)
of the Act and the case against the accused Nos.1 to 4 for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the IPC is pending before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court vide Criminal Case No.2256 of 2019 and as on today, the matter is pending for framing of charge.
6.1.

Learned APP has further submitted that so far as the present applicant is concerned, no charge-sheet is submitted as the investigation was not carried out so far as the involvement of the applicant in the commission of an offence and therefore, submitted that the petition may be dismissed and the applicant NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED:
12/12/2024 undefined may be directed to co-operate in the investigation process.

6.2. It is further submitted that the decision relied upon by the learned advocate for the applicant in the case Vipulkumar Avantilal Shah (supra) is not applicable as in the case before the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, charge-sheet was filed and after considering the material, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court observed that no ingredients to constitute the offence of criminal breach of trust or cheating are spelt out.
7. Having considered the submissions and the impugned FIR together with other material placed on record, the basic allegation in the complaint is that on a raid conducted by the complainant, accused No.1 was found to have an illegal stock exchange running in his shop and during the seizure of some material, more particularly, a note-book, name of accused Nos.2 to 5 are found and therefore, the present applicant is arraigned as accused No.5 in the impugned FIR.
The allegations made in the NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined impugned FIR are not covering any of the ingredients as contemplated in Section 420 of the IPC.

The provision of Section 420 of the IPC is reproduced hereunder for the sake of assistance:-
"Section 420:- Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security,
or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security

, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine."
8.

To invoke the provisions of Section 420, the allegations has to be to the effect that person who cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security.

When the FIR does not disclose about the basic ingredient of dishonestly inducing the person deceived to deliver any Kirtibhai Revabhai Patel Named In The ... vs State Of Gujarat on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153172755/

3 property to any person, it would be an abuse of the process of law if the NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined criminal proceedings against the present applicant is allowed to be undergone.

From the report dated 11.12.2014, it is coming out that the learned Sessions Court has discharged accused Nos.1 to 4 from the commission of an offence under Sections 19, 23(1)(c), (e), (f), (g), (i) of the Act and the case has been remitted back to the learned Magistrate to be proceeded for the offence under Section 420 of the Code against accused Nos.1 to 9.

The issue involved in the present application is no more res integra in the decision of Vipulkumar Avantilal Shah (supra), wherein, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court has, in paragraph Nos.8, 9, 10,
11 and 12, discussed the provision of Section 26 of the Act and also held that police has the power to investigate the offence alleged against the applicant.
The Court will not be able to take cognizance in view of the specific bar.
The investigation carried out by police can be used for the purpose of filing a complaint in writing before the appropriate Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 10.

It would be apposite to refer the decision in the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, the Apex Court has set out the categories of cases in which the inherent power under Section 482 CrPC can be exercised and held in para 102 as under:
"102.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this Court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Art. 226 or the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we give the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised :
"(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

(7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge

. "

4
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/441/2014 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 11.
Thus, in view of the settled position of law and in view of the above discussions, the present application is allowed.

The impugned FIR being I-C.R. No.2 of 2014 registered with Ranavav Police Station, District Porbandar for the offences punishable under Sections 420 of the Code read with Sections 19, 23(1)(c), (e), (f), (g), (i) of the Act as well as all consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof
are hereby quashed and set aside qua the applicant.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
